label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: the conductor, dev, deck, ruv-sgit, the researcher and the designer
findings.why: A newcomer meets six names, two of them odd (deck, ruv-sgit), with no hint of what each does before the hours begin.

findings.quote: the conductor set the pace and wrote the third edition of its night log, deck sent ruv-sgit its second experiment
findings.why: One sentence stacks four members' jobs with 'and', and I lose who did what and why it matters.

findings.quote: What the record shows is not whether everything finished
findings.why: This reads as a reporter describing the record, with no 'I' and no hindsight on why the editor cares.

findings.quote: Part four keeps all three, and asks what that order should have been.
findings.why: A pointer to a later part that a first-build reader cannot yet value, and it interrupts the scene.

findings.quote: a vault key (the key that opens one of the team's shared stores of files)
findings.why: The aside helps, but 'redacted' and 'captured pages' are never explained, so the failure itself stays vague to a non-coder.

findings.quote: Three rounds, one picture, and I started none of them.
findings.why: It restates the three rounds just told in lines 63-71 and then the figure at line 73 shows them a third time.

findings.quote: A piece marked ready for me, then another. A list of what waits on me
findings.why: A run of fragments and short sentences (lines 151-153) where one running thought would carry the idea of the queue at one door.

findings.quote: Nobody told it to this time. The members were pacing each other.
findings.why: Two short sentences after a short one; they could join into the thought about members pacing themselves.

findings.quote: If you try reading what they did first, before you ask for anything new
findings.why: It tells me how to behave, and the 'temptation' line above assumes I am the sort who would rush.

findings.quote: dropped the "@" from its name and the line saying which agent made them
findings.why: A first-build reader has no idea what the '@' or the agent trailer is for, so the lapse means nothing to me.

findings.quote: *How to read the scenes:* they are dramatised.
findings.why: It is an instruction on how to read, and it comes after the stops are already announced as 'the record'.

findings.quote: Chapter 3 walked four of these pages
findings.why: Line 2 already says chapter 3 has the first four stops, so the same pointer is told twice in a few lines.

findings.quote: If a fresh copy of me cannot rebuild it from the explainer and the data, it is not finished.
findings.why: 'A fresh copy of me' is the first moment I stall on what an agent is, and the glossary is a long way off.

findings.quote: The point is the receipt at the end of each
findings.why: A 'the point is' opening, and the line below repeats it as 'Never silent'.

findings.quote: The vaults page prints the vaults' read keys, so the book names it here once
findings.why: Vaults and read keys are never explained here, and this is the paragraph that tells me what I am not shown.

findings.quote: like one agent's that was still open when the hold came
findings.why: The one example leans on 'hold' and a particular agent I may not remember, so the definition stays unclear.

what_holds: 09-nine-hours-with-nobody-starting-work.md: the opening at lines 5 in the editor's own voice (my last word at 04:03, my next at ten to two) and the honest partial wakes make the nine hours feel human and believable.
09-nine-hours-with-nobody-starting-work.md: the designer owning its mistake (lines 129-131) and ruv-sgit's idle bench (line 168) are the moments I would tell someone about.
90-the-tour-at-length.md: each stop is short, with a picture and one line from its maker, so I can stop anywhere without losing the thread.
91-the-words-used.md: plain one-line definitions with the chapter named; this is the page I would use, especially agent, repository, commit and the check.
notes: As a first-build finisher I want the next step, and chapter 9 mostly shows a team that already works rather than how I would start; the closing 'Something to try' is the only handle and it is thin. The tour reads as a catalogue for readers who already know the factory. Most stops carry a repeated pattern of 'Narrator then one line', which becomes skimmable by stop 6.
